answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer: No, skip the 22-miler. Sun Oct 4 sits 14 days before the race, and the long run that close has to leave you fresh, not drain you. You already have a 20-miler in the bank from Sep 13 and a strong 17 last Sunday, which is plenty of long-run work for sub-3:45. The right move now is a 16-miler with marathon-pace running on the back half, then a real taper. That builds race-pace confidence without the recovery cost of a 22.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed

You executed every session as planned and the numbers back the goal. The 3 x 2 mi at 7:58/mi came in at 7/10 effort with no fade, and the 17-miler at 9:59/mi drifted only 5 bpm — both signs the engine is ready for 8:35/mi on race day.

## Why the long run comes down, not up

The race moved to Sun Oct 18, which puts your last long run 14 days out and your taper into a single week. A 22 now would eat into leg freshness and sleep without adding fitness that can show up by race day. Marathon fitness built over the last 12 weeks is already banked.

## What this week does instead

Wednesday is a short marathon-pace block to lock in the feel of 8:35/mi, and Sunday is the dress rehearsal: easy miles, then 6 at marathon pace on tired-ish legs. If 8:35 feels forced on Sunday, back off and run the race by effort — don't chase the number. After that, we drop volume next week while keeping a touch of pace work so your legs stay sharp.

## One ask

Treat the rest days as full rest, and keep sleep at seven-plus hours. The sharpening is done in recovery now, not in extra miles.
